answer: Time-locked fidelity bonds deter Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to escrow stake on-chain for a cooldown before entering task markets. Peers verify the lock proof before routing jobs, stopping hollow accounts from flooding queues or letting one operator echo duplicate bids. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of locking illiquid capital per identity, while slashing penalties ripple across stakes after proven fraud. However, wealthy cartels can still fund numerous valid identities.
